# Intro

[Broad institute code](https://github.com/broadinstitute/gtex-tutorials/blob/master/GTEx_data_tutorial_R.ipynb) was used as basis for analysis.

# Sample & donor metadata

Load GTEx annotation files.

```{r}
library(data.table)
sample.dt  <- fread("data/GTEx_Analysis_v11_Annotations_SampleAttributesDS.txt")
subject.dt <- fread("data/GTEx_Analysis_v11_Annotations_SubjectPhenotypesDS.txt")
```

Visualize GTEx annotation files. Note:

- SUBJID -\> unique subject ID

- SEX -\> 1 = male, 2 = female

- AGE -\> Decade

- DTHHARDY = Hardy scale -\> 0 = ventilator, 1 = violent and fast (\< 10 min), 2 = fast of natural causes (\< 1 hr), 3 = intermediate (1 - 24 hours), 4 = slow (\> 1 day)

```{r}
head(sample.dt, 5)
head(subject.dt, 5)

cat("Sample dimensions: ", dim(sample.dt), "\n")
cat("Subject dimensions: ", dim(subject.dt), "\n")
```

Build a new data table containing RNA-seq analysis freeze samples only. Appears that samples that *aren't* included in tissue expression data are initially included in the sample attributes annotations.

```{r}
rnaseq.sample.dt <- sample.dt[SMAFRZE == "RNASEQ"]

head(rnaseq.sample.dt, 5)
```

Within the GTEx sample annotations, the number of samples within each tissue site can be visualized

```{r}
# matrix(sort(table(rnaseq.sample.dt$SMTSD), decreasing=TRUE))
```

Prior to bring in the expression data, we can isolate relevant annotation information for our target tissue sites.

```{r}
blood.sample.dt = rnaseq.sample.dt[SMTSD == "Brain - Frontal Cortex (BA9)"]
cortex.sample.dt = rnaseq.sample.dt[SMTSD == "Brain - Cortex"]
```

# Import expression data

Remove .gct two-line header.

Optional: move description (gene ID) to gene variable to allow querying - might not be needed for data tables.

```{r}
blood.dt <- fread("data/gene_reads_adult_gtex_v11_whole_blood.gct", skip=2)
cortex.dt <- fread("data/gene_reads_adult_gtex_v11_brain_cortex.gct", skip=2)
```

Data info (note description row is included in genes now):

```{r}
head(blood.dt[,1:6]) # When rendered, all rows will be printed -> limit to 6
head(cortex.dt[,1:6])

cat("Whole-blood dimensions: ", dim(blood.dt), "\n")
cat("Brain-cortex dimensions: ", dim(cortex.dt), "\n")
```

# Cohort overlap

Build overlap and isolation datasets.

```{r}
# Subject annotation uses reduced donor ID
# Build function to remove non-uniform ID components
#   "GTEX-1117F-0005-SM-HL9SH"  ->  "GTEX-1117F"
donor_id <- function(x) {
  parts <- tstrsplit(x, "-", fixed = TRUE)  # split each ID into its fields
  paste(parts[[1]], parts[[2]], sep = "-")  # rejoin the first two = the donor
}

# Isolate donor IDs in each group
blood.donors  <- donor_id(blood.sample.dt$SAMPID)
cortex.donors <- donor_id(cortex.sample.dt$SAMPID)

# Split the donors into relevant groups
overlap.donors     <- intersect(blood.donors, cortex.donors)  # gave both tissues
blood.only.donors  <- setdiff(blood.donors,  cortex.donors)   # gave blood, not cortex
cortex.only.donors <- setdiff(cortex.donors, blood.donors)    # gave cortex, not blood

# Show sizes of each group
data.table(
  group   = c("Whole Blood", "Brain - Cortex", "Overlap (both)",
              "Blood only", "Cortex only"),
  n_donors = c(length(blood.donors), length(cortex.donors),
               length(overlap.donors), length(blood.only.donors),
               length(cortex.only.donors))
)

# Make venn diagram
library(eulerr)
region.counts <- c(
  Frontal          = length(blood.only.donors),
  Cortex         = length(cortex.only.donors),
  "Frontal&Cortex" = length(overlap.donors)
)

plot(euler(region.counts), quantities = TRUE, main = "Donors by tissue")
```

## Demographics

Covariate data: sex (1 = male, 2 = female), age (sorted by 10s), hardy scale.

Compare overlap with original sample distributions.

I reviewed the sample attributes and didn't see anything that would be relevant for selection bias control.

```{r}
# Label every donor with its group, then attach that donor's phenotypes.
# Create list w/ donor IDs and labeled group column x5 -> stack vertically with rbindlist
donor.groups <- rbindlist(list(
  data.table(group = "overlap",    SUBJID = overlap.donors),
  # data.table(group = "cortexOnly", SUBJID = cortex.only.donors),
  # data.table(group = "bloodOnly",  SUBJID = blood.only.donors),
  data.table(group = "cortex", SUBJID = cortex.donors),
  data.table(group = "blood", SUBJID = blood.donors)
))

# Attach covariate data from subject dataset
donor.groups <- subject.dt[donor.groups, on = "SUBJID"] #data.table join using key to add demographic info


# For each covariate -> print counts + normalized table -> stacked bar chart
library(ggplot2)
for (i in c("SEX", "AGE", "DTHHRDY")) {

  # Pull out the two columns we care about for this covariate
  work <- data.table(
    covariate = as.character(donor.groups[[i]]),  # the covariate value
    group = donor.groups$group                # which cohort the donor is in
  )

  # Count donors in each group-level combination (.N = rows in each bucket)
  counts <- work[, .(n = .N), by = .(group, covariate)]

  # Turn each count into a proportion of its group
  counts[, group_total := sum(n), by = group]     # total donors in the group
  counts[, prop := round(n / group_total, 3)]     # count / group total = share of group

  # Print counts + proportions side by side -> dcast pivots the long list into a wide grid
  cat("\n---", i, "---\n")
  print(dcast(counts, covariate ~ group, value.var = c("n", "prop"), fill = 0))

  # Plot
  p <- ggplot(counts, aes(x = group, y = prop, fill = covariate)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.75) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion within group", fill = i,
         title = paste("Composition by group -", i))
  print(p)
}

```

## Paired-donor subset for a matched comparison

One row per paired sample (blood + cortex for each overlap donor), with donor, tissue, and covariates in a single table -- the colData for a within-donor (paired) DESeq2 contrast (`~ SUBJID + tissue`) that controls donor-level confounders.

```{r}
# Grab the paired blood and cortex samples (donors present in both tissues)
blood.paired  <- blood.sample.dt [donor_id(SAMPID) %in% overlap.donors]
cortex.paired <- cortex.sample.dt[donor_id(SAMPID) %in% overlap.donors]

# Stack them into one table, keeping just the columns we need
paired.dt <- rbind(blood.paired, cortex.paired)
paired.dt <- paired.dt[, .(SAMPID, SUBJID = donor_id(SAMPID), tissue = SMTSD)]

# Attach donor phenotypes (SEX, AGE, DTHHRDY)
paired.dt <- subject.dt[paired.dt, on = "SUBJID"]

# Set column order + sort so each donor's two rows sit together
setcolorder(paired.dt, c("SAMPID", "SUBJID", "tissue", "SEX", "AGE", "DTHHRDY"))
setorder(paired.dt, SUBJID, tissue)

paired.dt
```

## Expression counts for the paired samples

The other half DESeq2 needs: a gene x sample count matrix. It stays a matrix (not a data table) because rows are genes and columns are samples -- a different shape from the per-sample `paired.dt`. The two are linked by matching `colnames(counts)` to `paired.dt$SAMPID`.

```{r}
# The paired sample IDs for each tissue
blood.samp  <- paired.dt[tissue == "Whole Blood",    SAMPID]
cortex.samp <- paired.dt[tissue == "Brain - Cortex", SAMPID]

# Both files share the same gene rows -> column-bind
counts <- cbind(as.matrix(blood.dt [, ..blood.samp]),
                as.matrix(cortex.dt[, ..cortex.samp]))
rownames(counts) <- blood.dt$Name # label rows with gene IDs

# Put columns in the same order as the colData rows
counts <- counts[, paired.dt$SAMPID]

dim(counts)
counts[1:5, 1:4]
```

Together, `counts` (expression) + `paired.dt` (colData) are everything a paired DESeq2 model needs: `DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(counts, as.data.frame(paired.dt), design = ~ SUBJID + tissue)`.
